t: Independent from 1821, Peru grew from the core of the Inca Empire and Spain’s Viceroyalty of Peru, with Lima as its capital.
Guano wealth funded railways and reforms, but defeat by Chile in the War of the Pacific cost it Tarapacá and Arica.
After military rule, hyperinflation and the Shining Path insurgency, it became a fast-growing mining economy with fragile politics.
dyk: From the 1840s to the 1870s Peru’s main export was guano, seabird droppings dug from offshore islands and shipped to Europe as fertiliser.
ev: José de San Martín proclaims Peruvian independence in Lima
Sucre defeats the last royalist field army at the Battle of Ayacucho
Ramón Castilla abolishes slavery and the Indian tribute
Peru enters the War of the Pacific against Chile
The Treaty of Ancón cedes Tarapacá to Chile
Juan Velasco Alvarado seizes power and begins radical reforms
Alberto Fujimori closes Congress; Abimael Guzmán is captured
Pedro Castillo is removed after trying to dissolve Congress
